findings.summary: The live overlay check compares only the four binding keys. On live rows, the old assertions bindingSha256==digest, reviewStatus=='pending' and whole-shard equality now run only at the authoring commit. Live edits to reviewStatus, bindingSha256, disposition, sourceContent or claimId go unnoticed, and so does the 136/5 disposition correction. The receipt overclaims that all earlier assertions remain.
findings.evidence: misc-fix/rebind.py check_live compares payload() only; rebind/rebind.py --check reports binding drift only. Reviewer controls on in-memory live ledgers: unrecorded payload edit on row 3 caught; row 2 reviewStatus=approved, row 2 disposition/sourceContent changed and row 2 bindingSha256 zeroed all pass.

findings.summary: rebind.py --check and verify.py leave /tmp/fgos-work/w11-misc-pin (misc/ and verify/) after every run, so the receipt's 'deleted' claim no longer holds.
findings.evidence: The scratch was present before this review (mtimes 02:15 and 02:26) and is rewritten by each check. No cleanup exists in rebind.extract or verify.main.

findings.summary: The vertical-list label rule only fires when an adjacent list line is also a witness. A lone glossed item that loses its single label in a longer list is not flagged.
findings.evidence: g9/w11-followup.py audit_glosses: vertical = vertical_label(before) and neighbors, where neighbors are witnesses at line +/-1.

findings.summary: recompose.workspace() can race between concurrent runs: the root is removed between FileExistsError and TemporaryDirectory, giving FileNotFoundError, or an empty root is left behind.
findings.evidence: g9/recompose.py workspace(): mkdir(parents=True) then try/except FileExistsError, and rmdir only if this process created the root.

findings.summary: The gloss on witness #2 calls the Stop-drain decision an open fork, then states its answer in the same parentheses.
findings.evidence: w10-gloss-audit.json witnesses[2].after; witness #0 shows the decision was answered on 2026-10-20.

Both Doer controls fail as expected, and the reviewer's unrecorded payload edit is caught.
